definitions.explanation: A large, stately house and its grounds. Often associated with historical residences of samurai, nobles, or wealthy families. Also used for large modern houses.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{屋敷|やしき}が{残|のこ}っている。
{武家|ぶけ}{屋敷|やしき}が{観光地|かんこうち}として{公開|こうかい}されている。
examples.english: A samurai residence is open to the public as a tourist attraction.

examples.japanese: {丘|おか}の{上|うえ}に{建|た}つ{広大|こうだい}な{屋敷|やしき}には、{庭園|ていえん}も{蔵|くら}もあった。
examples.english: The vast estate built on the hill had both a garden and a storehouse.

notes:
USAGE:
{屋敷|やしき} evokes a sense of size and historical importance. It is commonly associated with the residences of {武士|ぶし} (samurai) and {大名|だいみょう} (feudal lords) from the {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}. In modern usage, it can describe any impressively large house.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {邸宅|ていたく}: mansion, grand residence (more formal)
- {豪邸|ごうてい}: magnificent mansion (emphasizes luxury)
- {家|いえ}: house (general, neutral)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {武家|ぶけ}{屋敷|やしき}: samurai residence
- {大名|だいみょう}{屋敷|やしき}: daimyo estate
- お{化|ば}け{屋敷|やしき}: haunted house
- {屋敷|やしき}{跡|あと}: site of a former mansion
